academic_translation:
Now I must, by whatever means,
Undertake actions in accord with the family,
So that this flawless, noble family
Is not defiled—thus shall I act.
translation: Now I must do whatever I can to act in a way that fits this family. I will make sure I never stain this flawless and noble family.

academic_translation:
Even regarding a slight, ordinary thing,
Having intended in mind to give it,
Any person who does not give it—
If it is taught that they will become a hungry ghost,
translation: Suppose you decide in your mind to give away a small, ordinary thing. If you do not give it, the teachings say you will become a hungry ghost.

academic_translation:
Even the happiness of a single sentient being,
If destroying it leads to my own ruin,
For those who pervade all of space to its limits,
What need to speak of destroying the happiness of embodied beings?
translation: If destroying the happiness of just one living being ruins me, what will happen if I destroy the happiness of endless beings with bodies who fill all of space? I do not even need to ask.

academic_translation:
Therefore, just as I have vowed,
I must respectfully accomplish it.
If from today I do not apply diligence,
I will go lower and lower.
translation: Because of this, I must respectfully do what I vowed. If I do not make an effort starting today, I will go lower and lower.

academic_translation:
The appearance of a Tathāgata,
Faith, and obtaining a human body,
And such fitness to cultivate virtue—
Since they are rare, when will they be obtained?
translation: A Thus-Gone One appearing is very rare. Getting a human body, having trust, and being ready to do good deeds are also rare. When will I ever get these things?

academic_translation:
If I have not practiced virtues,
And have accumulated misdeeds,
For even a hundred ten-million eons,
I will not hear even the sound of the happy realms.
translation: If I do not do good deeds and I pile up harmful deeds, I will not hear even the sound of the happy realms for a billion great ages.

academic_translation:
If amiably served and honored,
all others bring benefit and happiness;
but if the afflictions are served,
they bring further suffering and harm.
translation: If I kindly serve and honor others, they bring me help and happiness. But if I serve my troubling emotions, they bring me further suffering and harm.

academic_translation:
Those wretched enemies made to suffer by natural death—
If even those who desire to forcefully destroy them when arrayed in battle,
Having disregarded the suffering of being struck by arrows, spears, and weapons,
Do not turn back and flee without accomplishing their goal,
translation: If even soldiers fight enemies who will die anyway, and ignore the suffering of being struck by arrows and spears, and do not run away before they reach their goal...

academic_translation:
The constant cause of all suffering—
Today, as I strive to destroy these definite natural enemies,
Whatever becomes the cause of hundreds of sufferings,
Needless to say, will not make me despair and lose heart.
translation: My true natural enemies are the constant cause of all suffering. Today, I am trying hard to destroy them. So of course I will not lose heart, even if this fight brings me hundreds of sufferings.

academic_translation:
If fishermen, outcastes, farmers, and so forth,
Thinking only of their own mere livelihood,
Endure the harms of cold, heat, and so forth,
Why should someone like me not endure them for the happiness of wandering beings?
translation: Fishermen, outcasts, farmers, and others only think about making a living. Yet they put up with the pain of cold and heat. I am working for the happiness of all beings. Why should someone like me not endure these things too?

academic_translation:
To liberate from afflictions the wandering beings
Who reach to the ends of space in the ten directions,
When I promised this, I myself
Was not freed from afflictions.
translation: I promised to free the beings who fill space in the ten directions. I promised to free them from their troubling emotions. But when I made this promise, I was not even free from my own troubling emotions!

academic_translation:
Without even knowing my own measure,
How am I not a madman to speak thus?
Therefore, in destroying afflictions,
I shall never turn back.
translation: Since I do not even know what I can really do, am I not crazy to talk like this? So I will never turn back from destroying my troubling emotions.

academic_translation:
I shall be attached to this,
And, holding a grudge, engage in battle;
Afflictions of such a kind
Are excepted from what is to be abandoned, since they destroy afflictions.
translation: I will hold tightly to this. I will hold a grudge and fight this battle! This is the only kind of troubling emotion I should not let go of, because it destroys all other troubling emotions.

academic_translation:
Where could fish and so forth
Be banished so that they are not killed?
From attaining the mind of renunciation,
The perfection of ethical discipline is explained.
translation: Where could fish and other animals be put so they are never killed? The perfection of good conduct is explained as coming from getting the mind of giving up.

academic_translation:
Unruly sentient beings are like space;
They can never be fully overcome.
If this single mind of anger is overcome,
It is as if all those enemies were overcome.
translation: Wild living beings are like space. They can never be fully defeated. But if this single mind of anger is defeated, it is like defeating all those enemies at once.

academic_translation:
Better that my gain and honor
And my body and livelihood perish,
And better that other virtues decline,
But I must never let my mind decline.
translation: It is better to lose my gain and honor. It is better to lose my body and the things I live on. It is even better to lose other good deeds. But I must never let my mind fail.

academic_translation:
This band of affliction thieves
Searches for an opportunity;
Having found an opportunity, they steal virtue,
And destroy even the life of a happy realm.
translation: This gang of thieves, made of troubling emotions, looks for a chance to strike. When they find it, they steal my good deeds. They even destroy life in a happy realm.

academic_translation:
From associating with a teacher,
And the instruction of a preceptor,
For fortunate ones who act with respect out of fear,
Mindfulness is easily generated.
translation: For lucky people who act with respect because they are afraid to do wrong, keeping in mind grows easily. This happens by spending time with a teacher and listening to the teacher who ordained me.

academic_translation:
When involved in dangers, festivities, and the like,
If one is unable, one should act at ease;
For it is taught that at times of generosity,
Ethical discipline is to be treated with equanimity.
translation: When I am caught up in danger, a festival, and the like, if I cannot keep up my practice, I should act at ease. It is taught that at times of giving, good conduct should be treated with even-mindedness.

academic_translation:
Desiring gain, honor, or fame,
Or desiring to seek attendants and retinue,
Or if my mind desires to be served,
At that time, I should remain like a log of wood.
translation: If I want gain, honor, or fame, or want to seek helpers and followers, or if my mind wants to be served, at that time I should stay like a log.

academic_translation:
Impatience, laziness, and fear,
And likewise impudence and idle chatter,
Or if a mind attached to my own side arises,
At that time, I should remain like a log of wood.
translation: If I feel impatience, laziness, fear, rudeness, or idle talk, or if my mind clings to my own side, at that time I should stay like a log.

academic_translation:
Regarding blameless things,
Governed by myself and sentient beings,
Like an emanation, without "I",
I should always hold this mind.
translation: For things that are free of blame, which are in my hands and in the hands of living beings, I must always hold my mind like a magical creation, with no 'I' in it.

academic_translation:
Having grasped this body as "mine,"
O mind, why do you guard it?
If you and this are separate,
What can it do for you?
translation: My mind, you hold onto this body and call it 'mine.' But why do you guard it so closely? If you and the body are separate, what can it really do for you?

academic_translation:
Thus, assume self-mastery, and
Always maintain a smiling face.
Completely abandon frowning and scowling;
Be a friend to wandering beings and speak sincerely.
translation: So, practice being in control of oneself and always keep a smiling face. Stop frowning and scowling completely. Be a friend to wandering beings and speak honestly.

academic_translation:
Whether motivated by constant, intense, fixed aspiration,
Or motivated by an antidote,
Toward the fields of good qualities and benefactors,
And those who are suffering, virtue becomes great.
translation: A good deed becomes very great when you do it with a strong, lasting wish, or when a remedy against troubling emotions moves you to act. This is true when you act toward people with good qualities, people who help you, and those in suffering.
